Capacity (MW).note: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists plant 10745 with these operating gas generators: steam generator BP15 at 13.4 MW, twelve gas turbines GT3 to GT14 at 87.1 MW each, and steam generator ST1 at 410.0 MW. That adds up to 1468.6 MW of nameplate capacity. The EIA table lists the 380.0 MW steam generator ST2 separately as standby, and GEM already carries it as unit 2. GEM's 1849 MW for unit 1 is 1468.6 plus 380.0, so ST2 is counted twice. EIA nameplate is the figure GEM records, not summer or winter ratings. The sum is my own addition of the table rows, so the value is implied rather than printed.

Status.note: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists BP15, GT3 to GT14 and ST1 at plant 10745 as operating. A Michigan regulator filing from August 2026 for Consumers Energy case U-22127 also describes a new power purchase agreement with this plant for 1,240 MW of dispatchable capacity. I found no retirement notice, planned retirement date or mothballing. A list kept by the Sierra Club shows this unit as terminated, but I did not cite it, and the EIA table shows no sign of that.

GEM lists it as fuel oil and mothballed. I found no dated source that says mothballed, retired or restarted, so status is left alone.
